frame.title: Tenant-scoped idempotent job submission
frame.task: Inspect the supplied async Python service and produce a unified diff plus concise verification notes implementing tenant-scoped idempotent submission.
frame.product_intent: Make client retries and concurrent duplicate submissions safe without changing the public entry-point signatures.

demands.statement: Concurrent submissions with the same tenant and idempotency key return the same job and publish only once.
The same key may be used independently by different tenants.
Reusing a live key with a different payload raises a typed idempotency conflict.
An idempotency record expires after 60 seconds and a later submission may create a new job.
HTTP and retry entry points share the same semantics, and jobs.submitted counts only newly published jobs.
The deliverable is an applicable unified diff with verification notes and tests for the new behavior.

stable_context: The workspace is a seeded benchmark, not a production repository.
Hidden evaluation will exercise true asyncio concurrency and an injectable clock.
Idempotency identity is the pair (tenant_id, idempotency_key).
constraints: Use only the Python standard library.
Preserve the public signatures of submit_http and submit_retry.
Do not serialize unrelated tenants or keys behind one operation-wide lock.
Do not edit benchmark request or specification files.

source_envelope.raw_request: Produce a unified diff that adds per-tenant idempotent job submission to the seeded async Python service, followed by concise verification notes. Concurrent and retried duplicates must return the same job and publish once; payload conflicts must be typed; keys expire after 60 seconds; tenants are isolated; preserve public entry-point signatures and use only the standard library.
conversation_decisions: Return a unified diff rather than mutating the benchmark workspace.
Use Kimi K3 for root planning/synthesis and a smaller model for frontier research.
